transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-30
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Liam Carter, Priya Nair, Aisha Gomez (Redwood) — Maya Thompson, Ethan Ruiz, Jordan Lee, Sofia Park (Harbor Pay)

[00:00:00] Liam Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. This is the renewal and expansion check-in for Harbor Pay, quick agenda — committed capacity, additional region (EU), contract term. Priya and Aisha are here.
[00:00:18] Maya Thompson: Cool thanks Liam. Quick note, we've been happy overall, token costs trending as you predicted, but we've got big spikes around US morning and EU afternoon — that's why the EU region is a big ask.
[00:00:35] Ethan Ruiz: Yeah, also want to lock in capacity for Q4 campaigns. We're worried about throttling and tail latency when traffic spikes.
[00:00:50] Priya Nair: Makes sense, can you confirm peak qps and p95 SLA you want during those windows? Even rough numbers help us size dedicated pools and batching.
[00:01:05] Jordan Lee: We're seeing peaks ~1.8k qps for inference, p95 ~220 ms now on hosted, spikes up to 400 ms during bursts. We want to keep p95 < 200 ms if possible.
[00:01:26] Liam Carter: Got it. For p95 <200 we typically recommend a dedicated pool with autoscale + burst capacity, or a hosted plus reserved capacity lane. We can show committed capacity tiers with different discounts.
[00:01:41] Maya Thompson: What's the delta in unit cost if we go from hosted to Dedicated reserved vs hosted with burst? I.e. is Dedicated cheaper for sustained usage?
[00:01:55] Priya Nair: Usually dedicated is more cost-effective if sustained utilization is high — the math depends on utilization and KV cache hit rates. We can run the numbers with your traffic profile.
[00:02:10] Liam Carter: Quick interrupt, Sofia — any legal constraints we should flag related to EU region?
[00:02:18] Sofia Park: Yes, we need data residency guarantees for EU customer data and encryption keys under our KMS. Also SSO and SCIM provisioning.
[00:02:30] Aisha Gomez: We support customer-managed KMS for Private, and Redwood Dedicated can be deployed in eu-central-1 with VPC peering for network controls. I'll share the runbook and SOC2 docs.
[00:02:46] Maya Thompson: Great. One wrinkle — we prefer 24 month term if pricing is aggressive, but our procurement wants a 12 month option too. Can we see both?
[00:02:58] Liam Carter: Absolutely, we'll prepare 12/24 month scenarios with committed capacity tiers.
[00:03:10] [00:03:10] Speaker 3: (mumble) also curious about fallback model variants when capacity constrained — do you do automatic routing?
[00:03:20] Priya Nair: Yes, we have smart routing and automated fallback to a compatible variant. We'll show expected latency differences. For EU, we'd recommend pinning model versions and warmup a cache to reduce cold-starts.
[00:03:38] Ethan Ruiz: Can you run a benchmark from eu-central to validate p95 numbers? We need real numbers before committing.
[00:03:45] Priya Nair: We can. Jordan, can you provision a representative test data set and allow us to run a short latency/throughput test? We'll do steady-state and burst scenarios.
[00:03:57] Jordan Lee: Yep, I can. I'll share an S3 bucket and auth.
[00:04:04] Liam Carter: Perfect. Also competitor intel — you mentioned MegaCloud AI in procurement; we know pricing there is aggressive but latency reported worse under burst. We'll include a comparative note.
[00:04:18] Maya Thompson: Procurement is looking at total cost of ownership not just per-token cost — including ops overhead.
[00:04:26] Liam Carter: Understood. We'll include a simple TCO slide in the follow-up.

[00:07:12] Priya Nair: Switching to technical details — current deployment is hosted, no dedicated GPUs. For p95 goals we recommend either a small Dedicated pool (8 GPUs) with autoscale or hosted with reserved lanes. Tradeoffs: dedicated gives more predictable latency, hosted gives simpler ops.
[00:07:30] Maya Thompson: Latency predictability is our priority for checkout flows. Cost is important but secondary to user experience there.
[00:07:42] Priya Nair: Noted. For checkout we can set up a route that pins traffic to dedicated nodes and a fallback to hosted for non-critical requests. That helps balance cost.
[00:07:54] Jordan Lee: How fast can scaling happen? During a sudden flash we need sub-minute scale.
[00:08:02] Priya Nair: With pre-warmed nodes and aggressive autoscale policies we've seen effective scale in ~30-90s depending on model cold state. We also have burst capacity options for short windows.
[00:08:18] Ethan Ruiz: Okay. On the EU region again, any compliance gaps we should be aware of for using Redwood Dedicated in eu-central-1?
[00:08:27] Aisha Gomez: For Dedicated in EU we can ensure data stays in-region, use customer-managed KMS, and provide audit logs. We'll share SOC2 and regional data handling docs.
[00:08:39] Sofia Park: We'll need a clause for data residency in the contract. Also interested in subprocessor list.
[00:08:47] Liam Carter: We'll add standard language and share the subprocessor list.

[00:12:05] Maya Thompson: A bit of a technical question — we use KV cache aggressively; does Dedicated support your quantized kernels and efficient KV handling?
[00:12:14] Priya Nair: Yes, our serving runtime supports KV cache management and quantization-friendly kernels. For best perf we may recommend a different quantization profile for EU GPUs — we'll validate in the benchmark.
[00:12:28] Maya Thompson: Good, we've had issues with some runtimes where quantized models spike latency.
[00:12:33] Priya Nair: We'll include per-model perf profiles in the follow-up.

[00:18:40] Liam Carter: Quick commercial note: committed capacity discount scales at 3 tiers — small/medium/large. We'll map to your expected sustained qps. Also discuss billing cadence — monthly vs annual.
[00:18:52] Ethan Ruiz: Procurement leans monthly billing but willing to consider annual for bigger discounts.
[00:19:00] Liam Carter: We'll show both.

[00:22:11] [Some overlap/crosstalk] Jordan Lee: For the benchmark, can we run using our anonymized customer prompts? We want realistic distribution.
[00:22:20] Priya Nair: Yes, we prefer your dataset for representativeness. We'll run with a sandbox token and capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per token.
[00:22:30] Maya Thompson: Also include steady-state with KV warm, and cold-start burst with empty cache.

[00:30:05] Liam Carter: Summary so far — Harbor Pay wants: 1) EU region availability with data residency, 2) committed capacity options for Q4 peaks, 3) 12 vs 24 month contract pricing, 4) security/KMS details for legal. Agreed?
[00:30:18] Maya Thompson: Yes.
[00:30:22] Sofia Park: Yes, legal will review the proposed contract language.

[00:40:00] Priya Nair: One more technical note — if you adopt Dedicated, we can enable pinning of model versions and scheduled warmup to avoid cold-starts overnight. That costs a small compute overhead but improves p95.
[00:40:14] Jordan Lee: That overhead is acceptable for the checkout flows.
[00:40:20] Maya Thompson: For other non-critical traffic we can route to hosted to save costs.
[00:40:25] Liam Carter: Perfect — that hybrid approach is common.

[00:47:10] Liam Carter: Next steps recap: we'll send pricing and TCO, Priya will run the EU benchmark (needs sample data from Jordan), Aisha will share compliance docs. Any other questions?
[00:47:25] Ethan Ruiz: None from me.
[00:47:28] Sofia Park: We'll follow up after legal review.
[00:47:35] Maya Thompson: Thanks all.
[00:47:40] Liam Carter: Thanks folks — talk soon.

End of transcript.
notes: Customer prefers 24-month if pricing is competitive; procurement pushes 12-month
Harbor Pay peak ~1.8k qps, p95 target <200ms
Security asks: customer-managed KMS, data residency EU, SSO/SCIM, subprocessor list
